editorial.headline: Berry Farming With a Clean National Opening
editorial.standfirst: This code covers berry cultivation from land preparation to postharvest work, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali PMA moratorium block on the record.
editorial.body:
Berry farming under this activity is not just the image of ripe fruit at harvest. The scope is broader and more agricultural: it covers the cultivation of berry crops such as blueberries, currants, gooseberries, kiwi, raspberries, strawberries, and other berries, including the full sequence of land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and postharvest activity when those steps are carried out as one chain of work.

The record also brings nursery and seed activity into the same frame. Planting berry crops to produce seed in the form of biji is included, as are pembibitan and pembenihan activities for berry plants. In practical registration terms, this makes the code suitable for operators whose business is centered on growing berry plants and managing the cultivation cycle itself, rather than treating cultivation, maintenance, harvest, and postharvest handling as disconnected activities.

The scale position is unusually straightforward. The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That means the slim record does not show a foreign-share cap below full ownership. A foreign-owned setup can therefore read the national position plainly: this activity is open, and the ceiling stated in the record is full foreign ownership.

The Bali position is just as clear, although it rests on a reason many founders do not expect. The provincial moratorium rule says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This record, however, marks the Bali status as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and says the OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is not that Bali is frictionless, and not that the moratorium is irrelevant. It is narrower and more useful: on this record, berry farming is nationally foreign-open at 100%, open across all listed scales, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium rule.
